**Meeting and packet.** Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, August 16, 2011, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Packet pages run 5 through 155. The consent agenda holds minutes of the June 21 and July 12, 2011 meetings, the Treasurer's Report for June and July 2011, and the diesel fuel bid award; separate items cover personnel, Schools of Choice under Section 105c, and the 2011 MASB Board of Directors' election.

**June 21, 2011 minutes.** President Philippart opened a public hearing on the preliminary 2011-2012 budget at 7:00 p.m., presented by Mr. Rajter and closed at 7:22 p.m. SET SEG presented a $1,250 Summer Leadership Camp scholarship to Athens High School; Dr. Don VanDenBerghe was recognized for 29 years of service. Resolutions 11-063 through 11-070 extended Superintendent Fowler's contract to June 30, 2014, extended assistant superintendent contracts to June 30, 2013 for Machesky, Keeling, Rajter and Witt, amended the 2010-11 budget, adopted the 2011-12 appropriations, and urged support for the August 2, 2011 Troy Public Library millage. Adjourned 9:05 p.m.

**Appropriations (Resolutions 11-068 and 11-069).**

| Fund | 2010-11 amended | 2011-12 adopted |
|---|---|---|
| General Fund | $138,268,519 | $128,282,487 |
| Special Revenue | 5,439,235 | 8,775,152 |
| Debt Service | 18,598,717 | 18,448,150 |
| Capital Project | 7,216,120 | 1,102,084 |
| Internal Service | 109,208 | 120,000 |

**2011-12 millage rates.** Non-homestead general operating 18.0000; commercial personal property general operating 11.4608; homestead general operating 5.4608; all properties debt retirement 4.7000.

**July 12, 2011 minutes.** Resolutions 11-071 through 11-081 covered administrative appointments of Anthony Morse (Boulan Park), David Pass (Troy Union) and Matt Jansen (Wass); MHSAA membership for six secondary schools from August 1, 2011 to July 31, 2012; a Section 105c resolution for the International Academy East; the second reading of the Code of Student Conduct; a laptop refresh totaling $1,804,916.25 charged to the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; and a call for the November 8, 2011 election of three members to terms ending December 31, 2017. Adjourned 8:45 p.m.

**Budget reports.** The June YTD FY2011 report shows General Fund actual revenue of $137,122,015 against actual expenditures of $137,177,728, an excess of revenue over expenditures of (57,191), and fund balance moving from 18,861,061 on July 1, 2010 to $18,803,870 on June 30, 2011. The July YTD FY2012 report opens the General Fund at 18,803,870 and projects (1,106,970) with a June 30, 2012 balance of $17,696,900.

**Action items.** Item 5.D extends Bid #9147 for diesel fuel with RKA Petroleum Company at an initial estimate of $385,000 on 160,000 estimated gallons, against $385,649.90 spent in 2010-11. Item 6.A approves probationary contracts for ten new teachers. Items 7.A and 7.B adopt Section 105c resolutions for ten 10th-grade seats in 2011-2012 and an unlimited number of 9th graders in 2012-2013 at the International Academy East. Item 10.A casts the district's MASB Region 8 ballot.

## Packet identity and agenda

Troy School District (City of Troy, County of Oakland, Michigan) Board of Education packet for the Regular Meeting of August 16, 2011, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Packet pages run 5 through 155. Agenda: Pledge; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; 5. General - Consent Agenda (A. Minutes of June 21, 2011; B. Minutes of July 12, 2011; C. Treasurer's Report - June and July, 2011; D. Bid Award for Diesel Fuel); 6. Personnel - Elementary and Secondary; 7. Curriculum - Schools of Choice, Section 105C for 10th grade 2011/2012 and 9th grade 2012/2013; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication; 10. Other - 2011 MASB Board of Directors' Election; 11. Adjournment.

## Minutes, June 21, 2011

Philippart opened a public hearing on the preliminary 2011-2012 budget at 7:00 p.m.; Rajter presented; the hearing closed at 7:22 p.m. Present: Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti, Underwood; Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Colligan, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Stromayer, Witt and VanDenBerghe; about 25 audience members. Thomas Longhway of SET SEG presented a $1,250 Summer Leadership Camp scholarship from the SET SEG Educational Foundation to Ms. Dixon and an Athens High Student Council representative, sponsored by the Michigan Association of Student Councils; Dr. Don VanDenBerghe was recognized for 29 years of service. Sue Martin, Bruce Bloomingdale and Ellen Hodorek spoke on the Troy Public Library millage.

Resolution 11-063 approved a consent agenda covering the April and May 2011 Treasurer's Report, minutes of May 3, May 12, May 17, the May 17 workshop and May 18, trash removal, CAD workstations and custodial chemicals (Ayes 6, Nays 0, Abstain Miletti). Resolution 11-064 extended the Superintendent's contract July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2014 (Ayes 7). Resolution 11-065 extended assistant superintendent contracts through June 30, 2013 for Richard M. Machesky (Secondary Instruction), Jan Keeling (Elementary Instruction), Mark Rajter (Business Services) and Jasen M. Witt (Human Resources). Resolution 11-066 extended administrative contracts through June 30, 2013 or as otherwise indicated, subject to the Administrative Handbook layoff provision, for Mark Dziatczak, Lara Dixon, Audra Melton, Timothy Fulcher, Janice Brzezinski, Lois Byrne, Brian Canfield, Jerry Cottone, Judith L. Garrett, Mary Haezebrouck, Jeremy Whan, Robert E. Dowd, Joseph Duda, Bettie A. Goss, Melissa Curth, James Johnson (June 30, 2012), Remo Roncone, Jennifer Gebbie, Amy Buchanan, Diane Kocenda, Michael Jolly, Kerry Birmingham, Kenneth Miller, Dominick Asaro, John Schiesler, Monica Papasian and Anne Mull. Resolution 11-067 gave Shawna Veit a two-year probationary contract as Supervisor, Special Education, effective July 1, 2011. Dr. Machesky gave a first reading of Code of Student Conduct revisions reviewed by the Board attorney.

Resolution 11-068 amended 2010-11 appropriations: General Fund $138,268,519; Special Revenue Funds 5,439,235; Debt Service Funds 18,598,717; Capital Project Funds 7,216,120; Internal Service Funds 109,208. Resolution 11-069 adopted 2011-12 appropriations and millage: General Fund $128,282,487; Special Revenue Funds 8,775,152; Debt Service funds 18,448,150; Capital Project Funds 1,102,084; Internal Service Funds 120,000; millage of 18.0000 mills non-homestead general operating, 11.4608 mills commercial personal property, 5.4608 mills homestead, and 4.7000 mills debt retirement on all properties (Ayes 7, Nays 0). Rajter reported the facilities study commences in fall 2011, facilitated by Mike Zinn, with a selection team of roughly 11 community members, a Facilities Study Team of about 25 to 35, and a presentation to the Board in February of 2012. Diversity Consultant Rosalind Cox reported 38 Diversity and Inclusion Council members. Resolution 11-070 urged support for the August 2, 2011 library millage vote. Adjourned 9:05 p.m.; minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

## Minutes, July 12, 2011

Called to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building with all seven members, Fowler, administrators Keeling, Rajter and Witt, and about 20 audience members. Resolution 11-071 approved minutes of June 7 and June 14, 2011 and the June 14 special workshop. Resolution 11-072 approved new hire Jennifer Doptis. Resolutions 11-073, 11-074 and 11-075 gave two-year probationary administrative contracts effective July 1, 2011 to Anthony Morse (Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School), David Pass (Principal, Troy Union Elementary) and Matt Jansen (Principal, Wass Elementary). Resolution 11-076 enrolled the district's six secondary schools in the Michigan High School Athletic Association from August 1, 2011 until July 31, 2012. A Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepted nonresident applications from counties whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries for the International Academy East; the school year prints in the source as 2010-2011. Resolution 11-077 appointed Katie Andrea and Cindy Desmon to the Oakland Schools Special Education Parent Advisory Committee for three years each. Resolution 11-078 approved the Code of Student Conduct on second reading, with Fowler noting hard copies would no longer be distributed and translation into approximately five of the most-used languages. Resolution 11-079 awarded a laptop refresh from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund: InaComp TSG (HP)/REMC $943,014.64; Apple/REMC-Apple Direct $534,628.72; Merit $155,652.24; Netech (Cisco)/MICTA $139,233.65; JAMF Software $8,000.00; CDWg/AEPA $24,387.00; total $1,804,916.25 (Ayes 6, Abstain Miletti). Resolution 11-080 continued summer tax collections for 2012-2013 with notice to the City of Troy. Resolution 11-081 called the November 8, 2011 election of three members to six-year terms ending December 31, 2017. Adjourned 8:45 p.m.

## Item 5.D - Bid Award #9147, Diesel Fuel

Memorandum of August 4, 2011 from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077, to Mark S. Rajter. The Board originally approved a diesel contract on June 15, 2004 for 2004/05; in July 2011 the district asked RKA Petroleum Company to extend through June 30, 2012 on the same terms and RKA agreed. Pricing rests on the lowest fixed profit margin per gallon: $0.0045 for regular diesel versus $0.0165 for the Macomb/Oakland Fuel Consortium. Estimated annual usage is 160,000 gallons; the recommendation is RKA Petroleum Company at an initial estimate of $385,000, against a 2010-11 diesel total of $385,649.90, as an expenditure of the 2011-12 General Fund. The attached RKA letter of July 26, 2011 from Chairman/Executive Director Keith L. Albertie proposes extending to July 31, 2012, cites certified minority business (WBE) status and BQ9000 Biodiesel Distributor certification from the National Biodiesel Board, and lists offices at 28340 Wick Road and 28340 Goddard Road, Romulus, MI 48174, (734) 946-2199.

## Item 6.A - Personnel, and Items 7.A, 7.B, 10.A

Probationary contracts for 2011-2012 are recommended for Mark Chrzanowski, 1.0 FTE PE/Health, International Academy East; Christopher Daugherty, .58 FTE History, International Academy East; Joseph Devault, 1.0 FTE ASD Teacher, Boulan Park Middle School; Stephanie Donelko, .5 FTE Chemistry, International Academy East; Meghan Hall, .4 FTE Social Studies, Athens High School; Gary Koskinen, 1.0 FTE Chemistry, Athens High School; Lindsay Kuroski, 1.0 FTE Social Worker, Special Education; Hannah Nagi, 1.0 FTE English, Athens High School; Natalie Selweski, 1.0 FTE Spanish, International Academy East; and Danielle Smit, 1.0 FTE English, Athens High School. Items 7.A and 7.B adopt Section 105c resolutions for ten (10) nonresident 10th grade students in 2011-2012 and an unlimited number of 9th grade students in 2012-2013 at the International Academy East, open to students from counties whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries. Item 10.A casts one Region 8 ballot for a three-year term on the Michigan Association of School Boards' Board of Directors among incumbent Donald Hubler (L'Anse Creuse Public Schools, Macomb County), Robert W. McLachlan (Romulus Community Schools, Wayne County) and Darlene L. Pomponio (Southgate Community Schools, Wayne County); ballots reached districts on July 22, 2011.
